evidence: Description of methodology

claim: Two model iterations were run: one with the three consolidated bat layers and the other with all the bat species layers considered separately.
source: Two model iterations were run: one with the three consolidated bat layers (i.e. Groups 1, 2 and 3) and the other with all the bat species layers considered separately.
evidence: Description of methodology

claim: The continuous suitability surface was converted into a binary at-risk versus not-at-risk surface by determining a threshold value that included 95% of the estimated suitability values of pixels with reported human index cases.
source: The continuous suitability surface was converted into a binary at-risk versus not-at-risk surface by determining a threshold value that included 95% of the estimated suitability values of pixels with reported human index cases (Pigott et al., 2015).
evidence: Description of methodology with citation to Pigott et al., 2015

claim: For sites represented by a specific latitude and longitude the suitability score was taken from the corresponding pixel.
source: For sites represented by a specific latitude and longitude the suitability score was taken from the corresponding pixel
evidence: Description of methodology

claim: For polygon estimates covering a number of cells, the mean suitability was taken across all pixels covered by the polygon.
source: for polygon estimates covering a number of cells, the mean suitability was taken across all pixels covered by the polygon.
evidence: Description of methodology

claim: Human population layers were not included directly as a covariate in the modelling process.
source: Whilst not included directly as a covariate in the modelling process, human population layers were assessed in at-risk locations as a potential proxy for spillover frequency.
